cross_references.note: §4553 enhancement applies to the post-apportionment compensation owed. If §4663 apportions 60% to industrial, the §4553 50% enhancement applies to that 60% — not to the full 100%. Apportionment reduces the base; misconduct premium then increases it.

§4553 enhances 'the amount of compensation otherwise recoverable' — this includes medical treatment costs under §4600. A §4553 petition paired with §4600(a) direct liability for self-procured treatment compounds the employer's exposure.

§3202 liberal construction applies to ambiguities in §4553 — including what constitutes 'managing representative' and what meets the 'serious and willful' threshold. Ambiguities resolved in worker's favor.

If the employer's serious and willful misconduct includes destruction or suppression of workers comp records (injury reports, WCAB filings), PC §135 is the criminal track. §4553 is the WCAB remedy; PC §135 is the criminal remedy. Both may apply simultaneously.

Systematic bad-faith denial of workers comp claims by the insurer may constitute both §4553 serious and willful misconduct (WCAB track) and INS §790.03 unfair claim settlement practices (CDI/court track). The WCAB has exclusive jurisdiction over workers comp claims; §790.03 is the parallel insurance regulatory track.
